headline: ECB HIKES 25BPS TO 2.25% — FIRST RATE RISE SINCE 2023 + US PPI 6.5% YOY DOUBLES DOWN ON METAL PRESSURE BEFORE FOMC
snippet: The European Central Bank raised its deposit facility rate 25 basis points to 2.25% at its June 11, 2026 meeting — the first ECB rate increase since 2023 — as euro area inflation hit 3.2% in May driven by Hormuz-disrupted energy prices that soared 10.9% year-on-year. The move lands on the same day the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported May PPI at +6.5% year-over-year, the highest since November 2022 and above the 6.4% consensus — a dual central bank tightening signal from both sides of the Atlantic that sent silver retreating to $63/oz (its lowest since December 2025), raised Fed October rate-hike odds to 40%, and compounds the pressure on precious metals entering Kevin Warsh's pivotal June 16–17 FOMC debut. For junior mining investors, the macro calculus now hinges on whether the Warsh dot plot frames this as a one-and-done or the start of a tightening cycle — a binary that will set the gold entry narrative for the rest of summer.

headline: CAMINO DRILLS 76.2m AT 0.88% Cu — 16.25m AT 2.67% Cu, ALL FIVE HOLES HIT AT PERU'S COSTA DE COBRE IOCG; 400m CORRIDOR OPEN
snippet: Camino Minerals Corporation (TSXV: COR) released June 10 Phase 2 assay results from the Adriana target within the Diva trend corridor at its Costa de Cobre IOCG Copper Project in Peru — all five reported drill holes intersected strong copper mineralization across a 400-metre strike length to a maximum depth of 260 metres, with the headline intercept of 76.2 metres at 0.88% Cu including a 16.25-metre high-grade core at 2.67% Cu and 6.82 g/t Ag. Costa de Cobre is a district-scale IOCG system developed in partnership with Japan's Nittetsu Mining Co., and the Phase 2 results extend the known Adriana mineralized footprint beyond the boundaries defined by Phase 1 (which returned 83.5m at 0.94% Cu in February); Camino now has over 28,000 metres of drilling completed across multiple discovery zones. With copper deficit forecasts ranging from 330,000 to 600,000 tonnes in 2026 and structural demand from electrification and data centres setting the multi-year price floor, IOCG systems in South America are increasingly strategic acquisition targets for the sector's next round of consolidation.

headline: ALKANE'S BODA-KAISER GROWS BEYOND 10 MOZ: MMT SURVEY DEFINES 6 NEW PORPHYRY TARGETS IN NSW — DISTRICT SCALE EMERGING
snippet: Alkane Resources Limited (ASX: ALK) released June 10 a regional exploration update for its Boda-Kaiser Gold-Copper Porphyry Project in Central West New South Wales, highlighting that a Mobile Magnetotellurics (MMT) survey flown north of the known deposits has defined six high-priority porphyry targets — Driell Creek, Murga, Gollan North, and three new prospects including One Tree and Old Station — each with the geophysical signature of an intrusive-hydrothermal system at depth comparable to the known deposits. Diamond core hole KAI226 simultaneously intersected a new magmatic root zone breccia at depth, returning 42.1 metres at 0.16 g/t Au and 0.14% Cu from 914 metres, confirming that the intrusive system footprint at Kaiser is larger than previously modelled. The Boda-Kaiser project already hosts a combined resource of approximately 10.3 million ounces of gold and 1.9 million tonnes of copper, making it one of the largest undeveloped gold-copper porphyry systems in Australia; the identification of six new same-signature targets at the district scale materially expands the exploration upside that a potential developer or acquirer must factor into their valuation.

headline: PROXY DEADLINE TOMORROW: ISS AND GLASS LEWIS BOTH BACK G2 GOLDFIELDS / G MINING DEAL — SHAREHOLDERS VOTE JUNE 16
snippet: G2 Goldfields Inc. (TSX: GTWO) announced June 9 that Glass Lewis & Co., joining Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) in recommending that G2 shareholders vote FOR the plan of arrangement with G Mining Ventures Corp. at the June 16, 2026 special meeting — with the proxy voting deadline falling tomorrow, June 12 at 10:00 a.m. Toronto time. Glass Lewis commented that the transaction emerged from a 'lengthy and robust strategic review process commenced in June 2023' and that the implied value represents 'a substantial premium over the Company's unaffected stock price and a fifteen-year high for the Company's shares.' The deal consolidates G2's high-grade Oko West Gold Project in Guyana with G Mining Ventures' operating Tocantinzinho mine in Brazil under a combined platform, with both ISS and Glass Lewis independently concluding the strategic rationale and governance process were sound — a dual advisory endorsement that historically drives over 90% shareholder approval rates in Canadian mining arrangements.

headline: JEFFERIES: "TURNS OUT WE WEREN'T BULLISH ENOUGH ON COPPER" — RAISES 2030 TARGET TO $8/LB, 491K-TONNE ANNUAL DEFICIT THROUGH DECADE
snippet: Jefferies analyst Christopher LaFemina published a June 9 note admitting the firm's prior copper forecasts were too conservative, raising the 2030 copper price target to $8 per pound ($17,636 per tonne) and projecting an average annual supply deficit of 491,000 tonnes through 2030 — driven by three forces not adequately priced in the firm's prior models: explosive AI data centre copper demand (each hyperscale facility requires 2–4 times the copper of a conventional data centre), grid buildout that is simultaneously pulling on the same constrained supply, and a structurally slower mine supply recovery than expected. Specifically, Jefferies lowered its combined 2026 output forecast for Grasberg (Indonesia) and Kamoa-Kakula (DRC) by 200,000 tonnes, with neither mine expected to return to full capacity until 2028; meanwhile, U.S. Section 232 copper tariffs are creating a persistent COMEX/LME premium that benefits North American producers regardless of the global price. For junior mining investors, Jefferies' four Buy-rated copper mining stocks represent their highest-conviction names to capture the structural decade-long deficit they are now explicitly conceding.

headline: ENERGY FUELS OPENS U.S. HEAVY REE FRONTIER: WHITE MESA CIRCUIT MODS START JULY — COMMERCIAL TERBIUM AND DYSPROSIUM BY Q4 2026
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU / TSX: EFR) announced June 11 that beginning in July 2026, the company will commence modifications to existing Phase 1 rare earth element circuits at its White Mesa Mill in Utah — the engineering work required to enable commercial-scale production of separated heavy rare earth oxides including terbium, dysprosium, samarium, europium, and gadolinium, targeting initial commercial HREE output by Q4 2026. Rare Earth Exchanges contextualizes the announcement as a potential breakthrough: Energy Fuels is currently the only U.S. company producing any quantity of separated HREEs from mined ore, and if the Q4 2026 timeline holds, it would establish the first domestic U.S. commercial heavy REE production at a moment when China's export licensing delays for MOFCOM-controlled HREE shipments are creating 8–10 week approval backlogs and dysprosium prices are up 105% year-to-date to $930/kg. The dual uranium-REE revenue model at White Mesa gives Energy Fuels exceptional optionality: the same mill infrastructure that produces uranium at a historic-low $9–12/lb processing cost can pivot to heavy REEs that today command premiums only available ex-China.

headline: CMR: BROKERAGES SEE 29–55% UPSIDE FROM HERE — JPM $6,000, WELLS $6,300, UBS $5,500 STILL INTACT DESPITE JUNE PULLBACK
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's early-June 2026 analysis frames gold's correction from $5,589 to ~$4,077 as a historically normal 27% pullback within a structural bull market rather than a cycle-ending breakdown, citing that corrections of 10–30% have characterized every major gold bull run including those of 2005–2007, 2009–2010, and 2019–2020 before subsequent multi-year advances. The piece surveys current institutional year-end 2026 gold targets — JPMorgan $6,000, Wells Fargo $6,100–$6,300, ANZ $5,600, UBS and Deutsche Bank clustering at $5,500–$6,200 — and argues that no major brokerage has revised its target downward despite the June correction, with the $4,400 200-day moving average and key Fibonacci support at $4,050–$4,100 defining the technical floor from which the next leg higher historically launches. For junior mining investors, the implication is stark: buying the June dip into FOMC week, when gold miners already trade at record profitability and decade-low P/E multiples, mirrors the 2003–2004 setup that preceded gold equities outperforming bullion 3:1 over the following 24 months.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD AND SILVER MINERS ARE "HIGHLY UNDERVALUED" — STRUCTURAL CASE FOR SECTOR OUTPERFORMANCE AS PAPER SELLING CREATES ENTRY
snippet: GoldSeek's June 2026 editorial argues that the current dislocation between gold mining equity valuations and underlying metal prices represents one of the sector's most compelling historical entry points — with gold producers generating record free cash flow at $4,000+/oz gold yet trading at implied multiples that assume gold prices well below current levels, creating an embedded margin-of-safety that has preceded every major sector re-rating since 2002. The analysis highlights that silver's structural six-year consecutive deficit (driven by solar, EV, and defence electronics demand) and gold's growing structural supply gap — Q1 2026 mine production fell 347 tonnes short of demand, requiring recycled metal to cover the gap — ensure that the physical fundamentals underpinning current prices are intact regardless of short-term paper-market repositioning ahead of FOMC. The editorial concludes that junior and intermediate gold-silver miners entering FOMC week are in the same setup as 2016 and 2018 post-correction lows: deeply oversold paper positioning, intact structural fundamentals, and institutional year-end targets 25–55% above current spot.

headline: SPROTT: LITHIUM ENTERS "NEW ERA" — EV STORAGE BOOM, POLICY SUPPORT, AND AI DATA CENTRES CREATE STRUCTURAL DEMAND FLOOR
snippet: Sprott's 2026 lithium analysis argues that the commodity has entered a structurally different demand regime than the 2021–2023 boom-bust cycle, with three overlapping demand pillars now simultaneously active: grid-scale battery energy storage systems absorbing surplus lithium capacity that EV demand alone cannot consume, AI data centre UPS and backup power requirements creating a new industrial lithium demand vector, and U.S., European, and Australian critical mineral policy frameworks providing producer-floor pricing mechanisms that partially insulate the market from China's cost-curve dominance. The piece contextualizes the 2025–2026 lithium price recovery (from <$14,000/t to >$24,000/t for lithium carbonate) as fundamentally different from the 2022 spike in that it is supply-shock driven (China's CATL Jianxiawo mine licence suspension) rather than demand-pull, creating a more sustainable price floor as Western hard-rock producers restart operations (MinRes's Bald Hill, Core Lithium's Finniss) at prices well above their all-in costs — establishing a competitive supply backstop to Chinese production that didn't exist in prior cycles.

headline: DIOS EXPLORATION WRAPS 2,024m ON QUEBEC'S AU33 GOLD — 10 HOLES ON HEBERTO SHEAR, ASSAYS TO ACTLAB; RESULTS INCOMING
snippet: Dios Exploration Inc. (TSXV: DOS) announced June 11 the completion of its 2026 follow-up diamond drill program on the AU33 Gold Project in Quebec, totalling 2,024 metres in 10 NQ holes — all targeting Heberto Gold extensions along gold-bearing silicified potassic altered shear zones at near-surface depths in a geologic corridor that has previously returned visible gold in core. All half-core samples have been shipped to Actlab for gold-silver fire assay, with results to be reported in batches as they are received; this is the first systematic follow-up to prior work that identified the Heberto structural trend as the primary gold host within AU33's broader 100%-owned land package. Given Quebec's Tier 1 mining jurisdiction status, existing road access, and proximity to established infrastructure, AU33 represents the type of high-optionality early-stage target that, with compelling assay results, could attract the disproportionate attention that underfollowed TSXV explorers typically see in active bull markets.
